 Essential skincare steps most people skip after turning 40
 Published : 26 October 2026
 • 
 Updated : 26 October 2026, 18:14
 • 
 FASHION & BEAUTY
 SHARE 
 K
 K T Humaira
 K T Humaira 
 Photo: Shahrear Kabir Heemel 
 If your mirror shows growing dryness and sagging despite trying every moisturiser, you might be missing the true culprit. Rebuilding your skin’s natural barrier — not buying ten different serums — is the missing key to youthful radiance. 
 Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source 
 Read more 8 tips to slow down ageing 
 What changes after 40 
 Your skin often becomes drier, thinner, and more sensitive as you age. This change occurs because your skin retains less moisture. A decrease in collagen production makes fine lines, sagging, and wrinkles more noticeable. Additionally, years of exposure to ultraviolet (UV) rays can lead to uneven pigmentation, a rough texture, and an increased risk of skin cancer.
 These changes are a normal part of ageing and do not warrant a harsh routine. In fact, mature skin typically benefits from less irritation and more consistency in care.
 Image 
 Photo: Collected / xandro Vandewalle / Unsplash 
 Sunscreen, EVERY DAY 
 This has turned into a cliché. Yet, people forget it every time they step out in the sun, or casually skip it because winter is coming. But to slow the ageing process and reduce the appearance of dark patches, it is essential to use a broad-spectrum, water-resistant sunscreen with an SPF of 30 or higher on all exposed areas.
 Read more Don’t skip sunscreen, even in winter 
 Apply sunscreen before going outside and reapply about every two hours while outdoors, or after heavy sweating. Additionally, seeking shade, sunglasses, and protective clothing can provide extra protection.
 Image 
 Photo: Collected / kimia kazemi / Unsplash 
 A gentle cleanser 
 To cleanse your face, use lukewarm water and a mild, fragrance-free cleanser. It is important to wash your face at night to remove sunscreen, makeup, sweat, and pollution. In the morning, a simple water rinse or a gentle cleanser is usually sufficient, especially for those with dry or sensitive skin. 
 Avoid harsh soaps and deodorant bars, as they can dry out your face.
 Read more Want younger skin? Here’s why salmon DNA could be the answer 
 A barrier-supporting moisturiser 
 If you are the one who picks up any cream from the supershop or sneaks moisturiser from your spouse’s vanity, “barrier-supporting moisturiser” might seem like a Hebrew word to you. It is more like a moisturiser that not only hydrates your outer layer, but also protects and rebuilds it — something essential after 40.  
 Apply it soon after washing, while skin is still slightly damp. Look for fragrance-free formulas with glycerine, hyaluronic acid, ceramides, or peptides.
 Read more Don’t let winter skin ruin your vibe — Follow this simple skincare 
 Retinoids and retinol 
 Over-the-counter retinol is a milder option that can help improve uneven tone, texture, pigmentation, and fine lines. Start at night with the lowest-strength product available. Apply a pea-sized amount to completely dry skin two nights a week for several weeks.
 Avoid the eyelids and the corners of the nose and mouth. It is also crucial to wear sunscreen every morning. Retinoids can increase sun sensitivity, and irritation may worsen discolouration.
